        """Find identities recurring across waves at a steady cadence.

        Shares every public input, parameter order and token semantic of
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_recurrences`, appending two further
        parameters, ``max_jitter`` and ``periodicity_limit``, validated
        in that order after ``recurrence_limit`` and still before any
        state is queried; ``max_jitter`` must be a non-``bool``
        :class:`int` (else :class:`TypeError`) of at least zero (else
        :class:`ValueError`), and ``periodicity_limit`` must be a
        non-``bool`` :class:`int` (else :class:`TypeError`) of at least
        one (else :class:`ValueError`). The same one frozen view captured
        by :meth:`_capture_frontier_view` answers the whole query, with
        exactly the same state checks, per-window node/change/lifetime
        caps, per-segment diff cap, total diff cap, wave qualification
        and ``wave_limit`` enforcement and single-read token
        reserve/refund semantics as :meth:`lifetime_churn_recurrences`;
        ``churn_limit``, ``streak_limit``, ``min_waves`` and
        ``recurrence_limit`` are accepted and validated identically but
        do not bound a periodicities query. The event graph, branch
        heads, audit and idempotency records and snapshots are never
        modified, and a tokenized success consumes exactly one read
        while any failure refunds it.

        The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
        ``periodicities, totals``. The complete wave set is built first
        with the exact semantics of :meth:`lifetime_churn_waves`; an
        identity appearing in at least three of those waves -- repeated
        churn within one wave still counts as the single wave it appears
        in -- keeps one record when the difference between its largest
        and smallest adjacent-wave gaps is at most ``max_jitter``, the
        gaps being the serial-number differences of consecutive
        participating waves. Each record keeps every field of the
        corresponding :meth:`lifetime_churn_recurrences` record in the
        same order -- ``type, identity, waves, first, last, span,
        segments, added, removed, changed, appearances`` -- and adds
        ``intervals, period, jitter``: ``intervals`` keeps, in
        appearance order, one fresh entry per adjacent-wave serial
        difference, ``period`` is the integer median of the sorted
        intervals (the smaller of the two middle values when the count
        is even), and ``jitter`` is the largest interval minus the
        smallest.

        Records sort by ``jitter`` ascending, then ``waves`` descending,
        then the summed ``segments`` descending, then the summed total
        change count descending, then ``first`` ascending, then the
        node, edge, gap type grouping and the identities' deterministic
        first-encounter order across the waves. ``totals`` is a fresh
        dict with keys ordered ``periodicities, waves, segments, added,
        removed, changed``: ``periodicities`` is the record count and
        the remaining counters sum every final record. Empty
        ``windows``, empty ``causes``, a batch with no qualifying wave
        or an identity set with no steady cadence return an empty
        ``periodicities`` tuple and six zero totals. The complete
        periodicity set is built before the ``periodicity_limit`` cap is
        enforced, so an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError`
        without truncating or returning partial records. Objects at
        every level are freshly built and share nothing with each other
        or internal state.
        """
        # Ordinary inputs are validated first, in exactly the existing
        # order, but no branch or historical node is looked up yet.
        validated = self._validate_frontier_inputs(
            reference,
            series,
            base_scenario,
            axis,
            values,
            min_size,
            max_size,
            required,
            exclusive_pairs,
            limit,
        )

        # The windows batch, the slice inputs and every existing cap --
        # including min_waves and recurrence_limit -- are checked exactly
        # as in lifetime_churn_recurrences; max_jitter (which may be zero)
        # and periodicity_limit follow in that order and still precede
        # every state lookup.
        point_count = self._frontier_point_count(validated)
        index_windows = self._validate_lifetime_windows(windows, point_count)

        causes, direction, depth_value, node_limit_value = (
            self._validate_slice_inputs(causes, direction, depth, node_limit)
        )
        change_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            change_limit, "change_limit"
        )
        lifetime_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            lifetime_limit, "lifetime_limit"
        )
        diff_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            diff_limit, "diff_limit"
        )
        window_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            window_limit, "window_limit"
        )
        total_diff_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            total_diff_limit, "total_diff_limit"
        )
        churn_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            churn_limit, "churn_limit"
        )
        streak_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            streak_limit, "streak_limit"
        )
        min_identities_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_identities, "min_identities"
        )
        wave_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            wave_limit, "wave_limit"
        )
        min_waves_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            min_waves, "min_waves"
        )
        recurrence_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            recurrence_limit, "recurrence_limit"
        )
        max_jitter_value = BranchStore._require_non_negative_limit(
            max_jitter, "max_jitter"
        )
        periodicity_limit_value = BranchStore._require_record_limit(
            periodicity_limit, "periodicity_limit"
        )
        if len(index_windows) > window_limit_value:
            raise ValueError(

                f"{len(index_windows)} windows, limit is "
                f"{window_limit_value}"

            validated,
            index_windows,
            causes,
            direction,
            depth_value,
            node_limit_value,
            change_limit_value,
            lifetime_limit_value,
            diff_limit_value,
            total_diff_limit_value,
            churn_limit_value,
            streak_limit_value,
            min_identities_value,
            wave_limit_value,
            token,
            "periodicities",
            min_waves_value,
            recurrence_limit_value,
            max_jitter_value,
            periodicity_limit_value,
        )

    def _run_lifetime_window_batch(
        self,
        validated: dict[str, object],
        index_windows: list[list[int]],
        causes: tuple[str, ...],
        direction: str,
        depth_value: int,
        node_limit_value: int,
        change_limit_value: int,
        lifetime_limit_value: int,
        diff_limit_value: int,
        total_diff_limit_value: int,
        churn_limit_value: int | None,
        streak_limit_value: int | None,
        min_identities_value: int | None,
        wave_limit_value: int | None,
        token: str | None,
        result_kind: str,
        min_waves_value: int | None = None,
        recurrence_limit_value: int | None = None,
        max_jitter_value: int | None = None,
        periodicity_limit_value: int | None = None,
        horizon_value: int | None = None,
        forecast_limit_value: int | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Build every window and adjacent segment on one frozen view.

        Shared by :meth:`lifetime_evolution`, :meth:`lifetime_churn`,
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_streaks`, :meth:`lifetime_churn_waves`,
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_recurrences`,
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_periodicities` and
        :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecasts` so all run the same state
        checks, caps and token reserve/refund semantics over one
        identical window batch. ``result_kind`` selects the assembled
        shape: ``"evolution"`` returns the ``windows``/``segments``
        dict and ignores every extra limit; ``"churn"`` returns the
        aggregated ``identities``/``totals`` dict, enforcing
        ``churn_limit_value`` only after every full record set is
        known; ``"streaks"`` returns the ``streaks``/``totals`` dict
        built from the same changes, enforcing ``streak_limit_value``
        only once every complete streak is known; ``"waves"`` returns
        the ``waves``/``totals`` dict of the consecutive-segment runs
        where at least ``min_identities_value`` distinct identities
        churn per segment, enforcing ``wave_limit_value`` only once
        every complete wave is known; ``"recurrences"`` builds that
        same complete wave set first and then returns the
        ``recurrences``/``totals`` dict of identities taking part in at
        least ``min_waves_value`` waves, enforcing
        ``recurrence_limit_value`` only once every complete record is
        known; ``"periodicities"`` builds the same complete wave set
        and then returns the ``periodicities``/``totals`` dict of the
        recurrences whose adjacent-wave gaps differ by at most
        ``max_jitter_value``, enforcing ``periodicity_limit_value``
        only once every complete record is known; and ``"forecasts"``
        builds that same complete periodicity set and then returns the
        ``forecasts``/``totals`` dict of candidate waves beyond the
        observation boundary within ``horizon_value``, enforcing
        ``forecast_limit_value`` against the total prediction count
        only once every complete prediction is known.
        """
        # Token checks come after every ordinary parameter. Without a token
        # the query runs on live state exactly as before; with one, the read
        # allowance is reserved atomically before any state check and given
        # back if a state check (KeyError/ValueError below) fails, so only
        # fully successful queries consume a read. Every window is then
        # answered from the token's one frozen view.
        view = self
        if token is not None:
            view = self._reserve_snapshot_read(token)
        try:
            # Capture the single read-only historical view once; every
            # window selects its snapshots and adjacent segments from it,
            # so the batch never reads different branch states per window.
            prepared = view._capture_frontier_view(validated)

            window_records: list[tuple[dict[str, object], ...]] = []
            for position, index_values in enumerate(index_windows):
                snapshots, segments = view._cascade_slice_timeline_data(
                    prepared,
                    index_values,
                    causes,
                    direction,
                    depth_value,
                    node_limit_value,
                    change_limit_value,
                )
                lifetimes = view._build_slice_lifetimes(snapshots, segments)
                if len(lifetimes) > lifetime_limit_value:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"lifetime {result_kind} lifetime limit exceeded: "
                        f"{len(lifetimes)} lifetime records on window at "
                        f"position {position}, limit is "
                        f"{lifetime_limit_value}"
                    )
                window_records.append(lifetimes)

            # Every segment's full change set is known before either cap is
            # enforced, so an over-cap batch returns no partial result.
            segment_changes: list[tuple[dict[str, object], ...]] = []
            total_changes = 0
            for position in range(len(window_records) - 1):
                changes = view._build_lifetime_changes(
                    window_records[position], window_records[position + 1]
                )
                if len(changes) > diff_limit_value:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"lifetime {result_kind} diff limit exceeded: "
                        f"{len(changes)} change records on segment between "
                        f"windows at positions {position} and {position + 1}, "
                        f"limit is {diff_limit_value}"
                    )
                total_changes += len(changes)
                segment_changes.append(changes)
            if total_changes > total_diff_limit_value:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"lifetime {result_kind} total diff limit exceeded: "
                    f"{total_changes} change records over "
                    f"{len(segment_changes)} segment(s), limit is "
                    f"{total_diff_limit_value}"
                )

            if result_kind == "churn":
                result = view._build_lifetime_churn_result(
                    window_records, segment_changes, churn_limit_value
                )
            elif result_kind == "streaks":
                result = view._build_lifetime_churn_streaks_result(
                    segment_changes, streak_limit_value
                )

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_waves_result(
        segment_changes: list[tuple[dict[str, object], ...]],
        min_identities_value: int,
        wave_limit_value: int | None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Group multi-identity churn into consecutive-segment waves.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_waves`. A segment qualifies
        when at least ``min_identities_value`` distinct node, edge or
        gap identities carry an ``added``, ``removed`` or ``changed``
        record on it -- one identity appearing several times on the same
        segment still counts once toward the threshold, while every
        change record feeds the counters. Each maximal run of
        consecutive qualifying segments forms one wave; a segment below
        the threshold cuts the run and the next qualifying segment
        starts a new wave.

        Every wave gets one fresh record with ordered keys ``from, to,
        segments, identities, added, removed, changed, members,
        changes``; ``from``/``to`` are the left window position of the
        run's first segment and the right window position of its last,
        ``members`` keeps one fresh ``type, identity, segments, added,
        removed, changed`` record per distinct identity sorted by
        segment count and total change count descending, then the
        identity's first segment in the wave ascending, then the node,
        edge, gap grouping and the wave's deterministic encounter order,
        and ``changes`` keeps one isolated ``from, to, kind, before,
        after`` entry per change record in segment and original change
        order. Waves sort by ``from`` then ``to`` ascending. The
        complete set is built before the ``wave_limit`` cap is enforced,
        so an over-limit query raises :class:`ValueError` without
        truncating or returning partial records.
        """
        type_order = {"node": 0, "edge": 1, "gap": 2}

        # A segment qualifies when its distinct churning identities
        # reach min_identities_value; qualifying runs of consecutive
        # segments become the waves.
        runs: list[list[int]] = []
        run: list[int] = []
        for position, changes in enumerate(segment_changes):
            distinct: dict[tuple[str, object], None] = {}
            for change in changes:
                type_name = change["kind"].split("_", 1)[0]
                distinct[(type_name, change["identity"])] = None
            if len(distinct) >= min_identities_value:
                run.append(position)
            elif run:
                runs.append(run)
                run = []
        if run:
            runs.append(run)

        waves: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        all_identities: dict[tuple[str, object], None] = {}
        total_added = 0
        total_removed = 0
        total_changed = 0
        for run_positions in runs:
            encounter: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
            first_segment: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
            member_segments: dict[tuple[str, object], set[int]] = {}
            member_added: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
            member_removed: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
            member_changed: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
            evidence: list[dict[str, object]] = []
            for position in run_positions:
                for change in segment_changes[position]:
                    type_name = change["kind"].split("_", 1)[0]
                    key = (type_name, change["identity"])
                    if key not in encounter:
                        encounter[key] = len(encounter)
                        first_segment[key] = position
                        member_segments[key] = set()
                        member_added[key] = 0
                        member_removed[key] = 0
                        member_changed[key] = 0
                        all_identities[key] = None
                    member_segments[key].add(position)
                    kind = change["kind"]
                    if kind.endswith("_added"):
                        member_added[key] += 1
                    elif kind.endswith("_removed"):
                        member_removed[key] += 1
                    else:
                        member_changed[key] += 1
                    before = change["before"]
                    after = change["after"]
                    evidence.append(
                        {
                            "from": position,
                            "to": position + 1,
                            "kind": kind,
                            "before": (
                                None
                                if before is None
                                else BranchStore._copy_lifetime_record(before)
                            ),
                            "after": (
                                None
                                if after is None
                                else BranchStore._copy_lifetime_record(after)
                            ),
                        }
                    )

            ordered_keys = sorted(
                encounter,
                key=lambda key: (
                    -len(member_segments[key]),
                    -(
                        member_added[key]
                        + member_removed[key]
                        + member_changed[key]
                    ),
                    first_segment[key],
                    type_order[key[0]],
                    encounter[key],
                ),
            )
            members = tuple(
                {
                    "type": key[0],
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(key[1]),
                    "segments": len(member_segments[key]),
                    "added": member_added[key],
                    "removed": member_removed[key],
                    "changed": member_changed[key],
                }
                for key in ordered_keys
            )
            wave_added = sum(member_added.values())
            wave_removed = sum(member_removed.values())
            wave_changed = sum(member_changed.values())
            total_added += wave_added
            total_removed += wave_removed
            total_changed += wave_changed
            waves.append(
                {
                    "from": run_positions[0],
                    "to": run_positions[-1] + 1,
                    "segments": len(run_positions),
                    "identities": len(members),
                    "added": wave_added,
                    "removed": wave_removed,
                    "changed": wave_changed,
                    "members": members,
                    "changes": tuple(evidence),
                }
            )

        waves.sort(key=lambda wave: (wave["from"], wave["to"]))
        if len(waves) > wave_limit_value:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn wave limit exceeded: {len(waves)} "
                f"wave records, limit is {wave_limit_value}"
            )
        return {
            "waves": tuple(waves),
            "totals": {
                "waves": len(waves),
                "identities": len(all_identities),
                "added": total_added,
                "removed": total_removed,
                "changed": total_changed,
            },
        }

    def _build_lifetime_churn_recurrences_result(
        wave_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        min_waves_value: int,
        recurrence_limit_value: int | None,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Aggregate, per identity, the waves in which it recurs.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_recurrences`. The waves are
        already the complete, ``from``/``to`` sorted result of
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_waves_result`, so each wave's
        position in the given tuple is the wave's serial number. Every
        wave member is one appearance; an identity that appears in at
        least ``min_waves_value`` waves keeps one fresh record with
        ordered keys ``type, identity, waves, first, last, span,
        segments, added, removed, changed, appearances``: ``first`` and
        ``last`` are wave serial numbers, ``span`` is
        ``last - first + 1``, the counters sum across the participating
        waves, and ``appearances`` keeps one fresh ``wave, from, to,
        segments, added, removed, changed`` dict per wave in ascending
        wave order. Records sort by participating-wave count, summed
        segment count and summed total change count descending, then
        ``first`` ascending, then the node, edge, gap grouping and the
        identities' deterministic first-encounter order across the
        waves. The complete set is built before the
        ``recurrence_limit`` cap is enforced, so an over-limit query
        raises :class:`ValueError` without returning partial records.
        """
        type_order = {"node": 0, "edge": 1, "gap": 2}
        encounter: dict[tuple[str, object], int] = {}
        next_encounter = 0
        appearances: dict[
            tuple[str, object], list[dict[str, object]]
        ] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(wave_records):
            for member in wave["members"]:
                key = (member["type"], member["identity"])
                if key not in encounter:
                    encounter[key] = next_encounter
                    next_encounter += 1
                appearances.setdefault(key, []).append(
                    {
                        "wave": serial,
                        "from": wave["from"],
                        "to": wave["to"],
                        "segments": member["segments"],
                        "added": member["added"],
                        "removed": member["removed"],
                        "changed": member["changed"],
                    }
                )

        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for key, wave_appearances in appearances.items():
            if len(wave_appearances) < min_waves_value:
                continue
            type_name, identity = key
            segment_count = sum(
                appearance["segments"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            added_count = sum(
                appearance["added"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            removed_count = sum(
                appearance["removed"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            changed_count = sum(
                appearance["changed"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            first = wave_appearances[0]["wave"]
            last = wave_appearances[-1]["wave"]
            records.append(
                {
                    "type": type_name,
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(identity),
                    "waves": len(wave_appearances),
                    "first": first,
                    "last": last,
                    "span": last - first + 1,
                    "segments": segment_count,
                    "added": added_count,
                    "removed": removed_count,
                    "changed": changed_count,
                    "appearances": tuple(wave_appearances),
                }
            )

        records.sort(
            key=lambda record: (
                -record["waves"],
                -record["segments"],
                -(
                    record["added"]
                    + record["removed"]
                    + record["changed"]
                ),
                record["first"],
                type_order[record["type"]],
                encounter[(record["type"], record["identity"])],
            )
        )
        if len(records) > recurrence_limit_value:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn recurrence limit exceeded: "
                f"{len(records)} recurrence records, limit is "
                f"{recurrence_limit_value}"
            )

        total_waves = 0
        total_segments = 0
        total_added = 0
        total_removed = 0
        total_changed = 0
        for record in records:
            total_waves += record["waves"]
            total_segments += record["segments"]
            total_added += record["added"]
            total_removed += record["removed"]
            total_changed += record["changed"]
        return {
            "recurrences": tuple(records),
            "totals": {
                "recurrences": len(records),
                "waves": total_waves,
                "segments": total_segments,
                "added": total_added,
                "removed": total_removed,
                "changed": total_changed,
            },
        }

        differences of consecutive participating waves, and the identity

        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_recurrences_result` field in the

        ``period`` is the integer median of the sorted intervals (the
        smaller of the two middle values for an even count) and
        ``jitter`` is the largest interval minus the smallest. Records
        sort by jitter ascending, then participating-wave count, summed
        segment count and summed total change count descending, then
        ``first`` ascending, then the node, edge, gap grouping and the
        identities' deterministic first-encounter order across the
        waves. The complete set is built before the

            tuple[str, object], list[dict[str, object]]
        ] = {}

                key = (member["type"], member["identity"])
                if key not in encounter:
                    encounter[key] = next_encounter
                    next_encounter += 1

                        "wave": serial,
                        "from": wave["from"],
                        "to": wave["to"],
                        "segments": member["segments"],
                        "added": member["added"],
                        "removed": member["removed"],
                        "changed": member["changed"],

            added_count = sum(
                appearance["added"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            removed_count = sum(
                appearance["removed"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            changed_count = sum(
                appearance["changed"] for appearance in wave_appearances
            )
            first = wave_appearances[0]["wave"]
            last = wave_appearances[-1]["wave"]
            records.append(
                {
                    "type": type_name,
                    "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(identity),
                    "waves": len(wave_appearances),
                    "first": first,
                    "last": last,
                    "span": last - first + 1,
                    "segments": segment_count,
                    "added": added_count,
                    "removed": removed_count,
                    "changed": changed_count,
                    "appearances": tuple(wave_appearances),
                    "intervals": intervals,
                    "period": period,
                    "jitter": jitter,
                }
            )

        records.sort(
            key=lambda record: (
                record["jitter"],
                -record["waves"],
                -record["segments"],
                -(
                    record["added"]
                    + record["removed"]
                    + record["changed"]
                ),
                record["first"],
                type_order[record["type"]],
                encounter[(record["type"], record["identity"])],
            )
        )
        # A None cap means a caller (the forecasts query) reuses the
        # complete periodicity set and enforces its own cap later.
        if (
            periodicity_limit_value is not None
            and len(records) > periodicity_limit_value
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn periodicity limit exceeded: "
                f"{len(records)} periodicity records, limit is "
                f"{periodicity_limit_value}"
            )

        total_waves = 0
        total_segments = 0
        total_added = 0
        total_removed = 0
        total_changed = 0
        for record in records:
            total_waves += record["waves"]
            total_segments += record["segments"]
            total_added += record["added"]
            total_removed += record["removed"]
            total_changed += record["changed"]
        return {

                "waves": total_waves,
                "segments": total_segments,
                "added": total_added,
                "removed": total_removed,
                "changed": total_changed,

21766	    @staticmethod
21767	    def _build_lifetime_changes(
21768	        left_lifetimes: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
21769	        right_lifetimes: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
21770	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
21771	        """Compare two windows' lifetime records type by type, by identity.
21772	
21773	        Records are grouped by nodes, then edges, then gaps; each group
21774	        runs removed, added and changed. Removed and changed records
21775	        follow the left window's identity order, added records the right
21776	        window's, so the output is stable. An identity present in both
21777	        windows changes when its first/last position, presence intervals
21778	        or classification transitions differ; a completely equal pair is
21779	        omitted. Every present side is copied again, so the change
21780	        records share no object with either returned lifetime tuple.
21781	        """
21782	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
21783	        for type_name in ("node", "edge", "gap"):
21784	            left_records = [
21785	                record
21786	                for record in left_lifetimes
21787	                if record["type"] == type_name
21788	            ]
21789	            right_records = [
21790	                record
21791	                for record in right_lifetimes
21792	                if record["type"] == type_name
21793	            ]
21794	            left_by_identity = {
21795	                record["identity"]: record for record in left_records
21796	            }
21797	            right_by_identity = {
21798	                record["identity"]: record for record in right_records
21799	            }
21800	            for record in left_records:
21801	                if record["identity"] not in right_by_identity:
21802	                    changes.append(
21803	                        {
21804	                            "kind": f"{type_name}_removed",
21805	                            "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
21806	                                record["identity"]
21807	                            ),
21808	                            "before": BranchStore._copy_lifetime_record(
21809	                                record
21810	                            ),
21811	                            "after": None,
21812	                        }
21813	                    )
21814	            for record in right_records:
21815	                if record["identity"] not in left_by_identity:
21816	                    changes.append(
21817	                        {
21818	                            "kind": f"{type_name}_added",
21819	                            "identity": BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(
21820	                                record["identity"]
21821	                            ),
21822	                            "before": None,
21823	                            "after": BranchStore._copy_lifetime_record(
21824	                                record
21825	                            ),
21826	                        }
21827	                    )
21828	            for record in left_records:
21829	                other = right_by_identity.get(record["identity"])
21830	                if other is None:
21831	                    continue
21832	                changed = (
21833	                    record["first_seen"] != other["first_seen"]
21834	                    or record["last_seen"] != other["last_seen"]
21835	                    or record["intervals"] != other["intervals"]
21836	                    or record["transitions"] != other["transitions"]
21837	                )

21844	                            ),

21847	                            ),

21850	                            ),
21851	                        }
21852	                    )

21865	        """Build the frozen per-index snapshots and adjacent segments.
21866	
21867	        Shared by :meth:`cascade_slice_timeline` and
21868	        :meth:`cascade_slice_lifetimes` so both read the same selected
21869	        snapshots and adjacent change segments from the one captured
21870	        view. Every input and state check has already run; an empty
21871	        index list selects nothing, an empty cause set yields an empty
21872	        slice per position, and the per-position node cap and the total
21873	        change cap are enforced before any result is assembled.
21874	        """
21875	        if not index_values:
21876	            # Every input and state check is done; no position is selected.
21877	            return (), ()
21878	
21879	        if not causes:
21880	            # Every input and state check is done; an empty set yields an

21882	            return (

32	    min_identities: int,

35	) -> dict[str, object]:
36	    """Independently project a reference periodicity set forward."""
37	    waves = reference_waves(evolution, min_identities)["waves"]
38	    boundary = len(waves) - 1

40	    periodicities = reference_periodicities(
41	        evolution, min_identities, max_jitter
42	    )["periodicities"]
43	
44	    records = []
45	    for record in periodicities:
46	        last = record["last"]
47	        period = record["period"]
48	        smallest = min(record["intervals"])
49	        largest = max(record["intervals"])
50	        predictions = []
51	        ordinal = 1
52	        while True:
53	            wave = last + ordinal * period

import copy
import inspect
import unittest

from city_twin.branches import BranchStore

from tests.test_lifetime_churn import churn_kwargs, diamond_store
from tests.test_lifetime_churn_waves import reference_waves
from tests.test_lifetime_churn_periodicities import (
    periodicities_kwargs,
    reference_periodicities,
)


def forecasts_kwargs(store_args, **overrides) -> dict:
    horizon = overrides.pop("horizon", 10)
    forecast_limit = overrides.pop("forecast_limit", 50)
    kwargs = periodicities_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    kwargs["horizon"] = horizon
    kwargs["forecast_limit"] = forecast_limit
    return kwargs


def forecasts_call(store, store_args, **overrides):
    return store.lifetime_churn_forecasts(
        **forecasts_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    )


def reference_forecasts(
    evolution: dict[str, object],
    min_identities: int,
    max_jitter: int,
    horizon: int,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Independently project a reference periodicity set forward."""
    waves = reference_waves(evolution, min_identities)["waves"]
    boundary = len(waves) - 1
    upper = boundary + horizon
    periodicities = reference_periodicities(
        evolution, min_identities, max_jitter
    )["periodicities"]

    records = []
    for record in periodicities:
        last = record["last"]
        period = record["period"]
        smallest = min(record["intervals"])
        largest = max(record["intervals"])
        predictions = []
        ordinal = 1
        while True:
            wave = last + ordinal * period
            if wave > upper:
                break
            if wave > boundary:
                predictions.append(
                    {
                        "ordinal": ordinal,
                        "wave": wave,
                        "earliest": last + ordinal * smallest,
                        "latest": last + ordinal * largest,
                    }
                )
            ordinal += 1
        if not predictions:
            continue
        projected = dict(record)
        projected["forecasts"] = tuple(predictions)
        records.append(projected)

    return {
        "forecasts": tuple(records),
        "totals": {
            "identities": len(records),
            "predictions": sum(len(r["forecasts"]) for r in records),
            "waves": sum(r["waves"] for r in records),
            "segments": sum(r["segments"] for r in records),
            "added": sum(r["added"] for r in records),
            "removed": sum(r["removed"] for r in records),
            "changed": sum(r["changed"] for r in records),
        },
    }

class LifetimeChurnForecastsResultTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):

    def evolution(self, **overrides):
        kwargs = churn_kwargs(self.args, **overrides)
        for name in (
            "churn_limit",
            "streak_limit",
            "min_identities",
            "wave_limit",
            "min_waves",
            "recurrence_limit",
            "max_jitter",
            "periodicity_limit",

            kwargs.pop(name, None)

    def test_matches_independent_projection_of_evolution(self):
        cases = (
            (((0,), (1,), (2,)), 1, 0, 1),
            (((0,), (1,), (2,)), 1, 2, 4),
            (((0,), (1,), (1,), (2,)), 1, 0, 2),
            (((0,), (1,), (1,), (2,), (2,), (0,)), 1, 0, 1),
            (((0,), (1,), (1,), (2,), (2,), (0,)), 1, 0, 3),
            (((0,), (1,), (1,), (2,), (2,), (0,)), 1, 1, 5),
            (
                ((0,), (1,), (1,), (2,), (2,), (0,), (0,), (1,)),
                1,
                0,

            (

    def test_predictions_respect_the_global_boundary(self):
        from tests.test_lifetime_churn_waves import waves_call

        windows = (
            (0,), (1,), (1,), (2,), (2,), (0,), (0,), (1,),
        )

class LifetimeChurnForecastsGroupingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @staticmethod
    def _member(kind, identity, segments=1, added=0, removed=0, changed=0):
        return {
            "type": kind,
            "identity": identity,
            "segments": segments,
            "added": added,
            "removed": removed,
            "changed": changed,
        }

    def _wave(self, serial, members):
        return {
            "from": serial * 2,
            "to": serial * 2 + 1,
            "segments": 1,
            "identities": len(members),
            "added": sum(m["added"] for m in members),
            "removed": sum(m["removed"] for m in members),
            "changed": sum(m["changed"] for m in members),
            "members": tuple(members),
            "changes": (),
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _periodicity(waves, identity="A", type_name="node", **counts):
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result(
            waves, 100, None
        )
        by_identity = {
            (r["type"], r["identity"]): r
            for r in result["periodicities"]
        }
        return by_identity[(type_name, identity)]

    def test_wave_ordinal_and_earliest_latest_formulas(self):
        # last 2, period 2 with steady intervals (2, 2): candidates
        # 4 and 6 inside a horizon of five (upper bound 7).
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "Z1"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "Z3"),)),
            self._wave(4, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        record = self._periodicity(waves)
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 3, 100
        )
        forecasts = result["forecasts"][0]["forecasts"]
        self.assertEqual(
            forecasts,
            (
                {"ordinal": 1, "wave": 6, "earliest": 6, "latest": 6},
            ),
        )
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 5, 100
        )
        forecasts = result["forecasts"][0]["forecasts"]
        self.assertEqual(
            [(p["ordinal"], p["wave"]) for p in forecasts],
            [(1, 6), (2, 8)],
        )

    def test_jitter_spreads_earliest_and_latest(self):
        # A at waves 0, 1, 4 -> intervals (1, 3), period is the lower
        # median of the sorted pair, one; last is 4. Candidates advance
        # by one while earliest/latest use the smallest/largest gap.
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("node", "Z1"),
            )),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "Z2"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "Z3"),)),
            self._wave(4, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("node", "Z4"),
            )),
        )
        record = self._periodicity(waves)
        self.assertEqual(record["intervals"], (1, 3))
        self.assertEqual(record["period"], 1)
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 2, 100
        )
        forecasts = result["forecasts"][0]["forecasts"]
        self.assertEqual(
            [(p["ordinal"], p["wave"]) for p in forecasts],
            [(1, 5), (2, 6)],
        )
        # latest is free to run past the horizon upper bound.
        self.assertEqual(
            [(p["earliest"], p["latest"]) for p in forecasts],
            [(5, 7), (6, 10)],
        )

    def test_candidates_at_or_before_boundary_keep_ordinal_numbering(self):
        # A synthetic record last seen at wave 1 with a steady period
        # of two; the observation boundary is wave 4. The ordinal-one
        # candidate (wave 3) is not beyond the boundary, so it is
        # skipped, but ordinal numbering is not restarted: the first
        # kept prediction is ordinal two.
        record = {
            "type": "node",
            "identity": "A",
            "waves": 3,
            "first": 0,
            "last": 1,
            "span": 2,
            "segments": 3,
            "added": 0,
            "removed": 0,
            "changed": 3,
            "appearances": (),
            "intervals": (2, 2),
            "period": 2,
            "jitter": 0,
        }
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 2, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(result["forecasts"]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                (p["ordinal"], p["wave"], p["earliest"], p["latest"])
                for p in result["forecasts"][0]["forecasts"]
            ],
            [(2, 5, 5, 5)],
        )

    def test_last_before_boundary_with_large_period_is_dropped(self):
        # Last seen at wave 0, period four, boundary 4, horizon two:
        # ordinal one lands on wave 4 (not strictly beyond the
        # boundary) and ordinal two on wave 8 (past the upper bound
        # 6), so no candidate is in range and the identity is dropped.
        record = {
            "type": "node",
            "identity": "A",
            "waves": 3,
            "first": 0,
            "last": 0,
            "span": 1,
            "segments": 3,
            "added": 0,
            "removed": 0,
            "changed": 3,
            "appearances": (),
            "intervals": (4, 4),
            "period": 4,
            "jitter": 0,
        }
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 2, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["forecasts"], ())
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["identities"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["predictions"], 0)

    def test_identity_without_an_in_range_candidate_is_dropped(self):
        waves = tuple(
            self._wave(
                serial,
                (self._member("node", "A"),)
                if serial in (0, 2, 4)
                else (self._member("node", f"Z{serial}"),),
            )
            for serial in range(5)
        )
        record = self._periodicity(waves)
        self.assertEqual((record["last"], record["period"]), (4, 2))
        # Boundary 4, horizon one: the first candidate is wave 6, past
        # the upper bound 5 -- the identity must not be selected.
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 4, 1, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["forecasts"], ())
        self.assertEqual(
            result["totals"],
            {
                "identities": 0,
                "predictions": 0,
                "waves": 0,
                "segments": 0,
                "added": 0,
                "removed": 0,
                "changed": 0,
            },
        )

    def test_empty_periodicity_set_yields_seven_zeros(self):
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (), -1, 5, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["forecasts"], ())
        self.assertEqual(
            result["totals"],
            {
                "identities": 0,
                "predictions": 0,
                "waves": 0,
                "segments": 0,
                "added": 0,
                "removed": 0,
                "changed": 0,
            },
        )

    def test_records_keep_periodicity_order_and_all_fields(self):
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (
                self._member("node", "A", changed=1),
                self._member("edge", "B", changed=1),
            )),
            self._wave(1, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("edge", "B"),
            )),
            self._wave(2, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("edge", "B"),
            )),
        )
        periodicity_result = (
            BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result(
                waves, 0, None
            )
        )
        records = periodicity_result["periodicities"]
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            records, 2, 2, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [(r["type"], r["identity"]) for r in result["forecasts"]],
            [(r["type"], r["identity"]) for r in records],
        )
        for projected, source in zip(result["forecasts"], records):
            for key in (
                "type",
                "identity",
                "waves",
                "first",
                "last",
                "span",
                "segments",
                "added",
                "removed",
                "changed",
                "appearances",
                "intervals",
                "period",
                "jitter",
            ):
                self.assertEqual(projected[key], source[key])

    def test_totals_count_predictions_and_historical_evidence(self):
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (
                self._member("node", "A", added=1),
                self._member("edge", "B", removed=1),
            )),
            self._wave(1, (
                self._member("node", "A", changed=2),
                self._member("edge", "B"),
            )),
            self._wave(2, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("edge", "B"),
            )),
        )
        periodicities = (
            BranchStore
            ._build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result(waves, 0, None)
            ["periodicities"]
        )
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            periodicities, 2, 2, 100
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["identities"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["predictions"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["waves"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["segments"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["added"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["removed"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["totals"]["changed"], 2)

    def test_forecast_limit_counts_predictions_not_identities(self):
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("node", "B"),
            )),
            self._wave(1, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("node", "B"),
            )),
            self._wave(2, (
                self._member("node", "A"),
                self._member("node", "B"),
            )),
        )
        periodicities = (
            BranchStore
            ._build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result(waves, 0, None)
            ["periodicities"]
        )
        # Two identities, one prediction each: two identities exceed a
        # cap of one only when predictions, not identities, are counted.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
                periodicities, 2, 1, 1
            )
        self.assertIn("forecast limit", str(caught.exception))
        # One prediction per identity fits a cap of two even though the
        # cap equals the identity count.
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            periodicities, 2, 1, 2
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(result["forecasts"]), 2)
        # A wider horizon yields four predictions and trips the same
        # cap even though the identity count is unchanged.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
                periodicities, 2, 2, 2
            )

    def test_output_shares_no_object_with_the_periodicity_input(self):
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        record = self._periodicity(waves)
        result = BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
            (record,), 2, 2, 100
        )
        projected = result["forecasts"][0]
        self.assertIsNot(projected, record)
        self.assertIsNot(projected["appearances"], record["appearances"])
        self.assertIsNot(projected["intervals"], record["intervals"])
        for projected_appearance, source_appearance in zip(
            projected["appearances"], record["appearances"]
        ):
            self.assertIsNot(projected_appearance, source_appearance)
        record["intervals"] = (99,)
        record["appearances"][0]["wave"] = 99
        record["period"] = 99
        self.assertEqual(projected["intervals"], (1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(projected["period"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(projected["appearances"][0]["wave"], 0)


class LifetimeChurnForecastsLimitValidationTests(unittest.TestCase):

import copy
import inspect
import unittest

from city_twin.branches import BranchStore
from city_twin.event_graph import EventGraph


def diamond_store() -> tuple[BranchStore, tuple]:
    """Three aligned checkpoints; prefix 1 is a0 only, later prefixes add W.

    a0 reaches merge W over a cross-branch convergence edge; the third
    checkpoint changes nothing, so the last segment carries only
    position-shift changes.
    """
    graph = EventGraph()
    graph.add("root", 0, (), {})
    store = BranchStore(graph)
    store.create("main", "root")
    store.create("a", "root")
    store.append("main", "r0", 1, {})
    store.append("a", "a0", 2, {"x": 2})
    store.append("main", "r1", 3, {})
    store.create("b", "a0")
    store.append("b", "bu", 4, {})
    store.create("c", "a0")
    store.append("c", "cv", 4, {})
    store.merge("b", "c", "W", 5, {"y": 8})
    store.append("main", "r2", 6, {})
    series = {
        "a": (("r0", "a0"), ("r1", "a0"), ("r2", "a0")),
        "b": (("r0", "a0"), ("r1", "W"), ("r2", "W")),
    }
    scenario = {
        "weights": {"x": 1, "y": 1},
        "total_budget": 20,
        "key_budgets": {},
    }
    args = ("main", series, scenario, "total_budget", (0, 10, 20), 0, 2, (), (), 10)
    return store, args


def churn_kwargs(store_args, **overrides) -> dict:
    _, series, scenario, axis, values, mn, mx, req, excl, limit = store_args
    kwargs = dict(
        reference="main",
        series=series,
        base_scenario=scenario,
        axis=axis,
        values=values,
        min_size=mn,
        max_size=mx,
        required=req,
        exclusive_pairs=excl,
        limit=limit,
        windows=((0,), (1,), (2,)),
        causes=("a0",),
        direction="both",
        depth=99,
        node_limit=50,
        change_limit=50,
        lifetime_limit=50,
        diff_limit=50,
        window_limit=50,
        total_diff_limit=50,
        churn_limit=50,
    )
    kwargs.update(overrides)
    return kwargs


def churn_call(store, store_args, **overrides):
    return store.lifetime_churn(**churn_kwargs(store_args, **overrides))


def reference_churn(evolution: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Independently aggregate a lifetime_evolution result for comparison."""
    encounter: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    next_encounter = 0
    present: dict[tuple, list[int]] = {}
    for window in evolution["windows"]:
        position = window["position"]
        for record in window["lifetimes"]:
            key = (record["type"], record["identity"])
            if key not in encounter:
                encounter[key] = next_encounter
                next_encounter += 1
                present[key] = []
            present[key].append(position)

    added: dict[tuple, int] = {}

    changed: dict[tuple, int] = {}

        and a tokenized success consumes exactly one read while any
        failure refunds it.

        complete wave serial numbers: at a cutoff ``c`` the periodicity
        set and forecast candidates are generated by the existing rules

    @staticmethod
    def _build_lifetime_churn_backtests_result(
        wave_records: tuple[dict[str, object], ...],
        cutoff_values: list[int],
        max_jitter_value: int,
        horizon_value: int,
        forecast_limit_value: int,
        backtest_limit_value: int,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Backtest each cutoff's forecasts against the waves after it.

        Used only by :meth:`lifetime_churn_forecast_backtests`. The
        given waves are the complete, ``from``/``to`` sorted observed
        wave set, so each wave's tuple position is its serial number and
        the last serial is the observation boundary. ``cutoff_values``
        are already type-checked; here they must each be non-negative,
        strictly increasing and name an existing wave serial, so a
        negative, duplicate, non-increasing or out-of-range cutoff
        raises :class:`ValueError` on the frozen view.

        At cutoff ``c`` only the waves with serial at most ``c`` train:
        the steady-cadence set and candidate waves are rebuilt by
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result` and
        :meth:`_build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result` with boundary
        ``c``, so later waves are pure observations and
        ``forecast_limit_value`` applies per cutoff exactly as in a live
        forecast. Every candidate is then compared with the identity's
        first later observed wave: an appearance at the predicted wave
        is ``hit``, before it (down to ``earliest``) is ``early`` and
        after it (up to ``latest``) is ``late``; no appearance in a
        fully observed interval is ``missed``, while an interval whose
        ``latest`` passes the last observed wave stays ``unresolved``.
        Outcomes keep the periodicity records' order and ascending
        ``ordinal`` within a record; ``actual`` is the matched wave
        serial for hit/early/late and ``None`` otherwise. The complete
        prediction set over every cutoff is built before
        ``backtest_limit_value`` is enforced, so an over-limit query
        raises :class:`ValueError` without truncation. Every returned
        object is fresh and shares nothing with the wave records or any
        other returned level.
        """
        observed_count = len(wave_records)
        final_serial = observed_count - 1

        previous: int | None = None
        for position, cutoff in enumerate(cutoff_values):
            if cutoff < 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"cutoffs[{position}] must be non-negative"
                )
            if previous is not None and cutoff <= previous:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"cutoffs[{position}] cutoff {cutoff} must be "
                    f"strictly greater than the previous cutoff {previous}"
                )
            previous = cutoff
        for position, cutoff in enumerate(cutoff_values):
            if cutoff >= observed_count:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"cutoffs[{position}] cutoff {cutoff} is out of "
                    f"range for {observed_count} observed wave(s)"
                )

        # Every observed wave member, keyed by type and identity, lists
        # the wave serials the identity appears in ascending order.
        observed: dict[tuple[str, object], list[int]] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(wave_records):
            for member in wave["members"]:
                observed.setdefault(
                    (member["type"], member["identity"]), []
                ).append(serial)

        zero_totals = {
            "predictions": 0,
            "hit": 0,
            "early": 0,
            "late": 0,
            "missed": 0,
            "unresolved": 0,
        }
        backtests: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        global_totals = dict(zero_totals)
        total_predictions = 0
        for cutoff in cutoff_values:
            training = wave_records[: cutoff + 1]
            periodicities_result = (
                BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_periodicities_result(
                    training,
                    max_jitter_value,
                    None,
                )
            )
            forecasts_result = (
                BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_forecasts_result(
                    periodicities_result["periodicities"],
                    cutoff,
                    horizon_value,
                    forecast_limit_value,
                )
            )

            outcomes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
            cutoff_totals = dict(zero_totals)
            for record in forecasts_result["forecasts"]:
                type_name = record["type"]
                identity = record["identity"]
                appearances = observed.get((type_name, identity), ())
                for prediction in record["forecasts"]:
                    predicted = prediction["wave"]
                    earliest = prediction["earliest"]
                    latest = prediction["latest"]

                    # Only the first observed wave at or after the
                    # interval's earliest edge can settle the
                    # prediction; an earlier reappearance lies outside
                    # the projected interval and never matches.
                    match: int | None = None
                    for serial in appearances:
                        if serial >= earliest:
                            if serial <= latest:
                                match = serial
                            break

                    actual: int | None
                    if match is not None:
                        if match == predicted:
                            status = "hit"
                        elif match < predicted:
                            status = "early"
                        else:
                            status = "late"
                        actual = match
                    elif latest <= final_serial:
                        status = "missed"
                        actual = None
                    else:
                        status = "unresolved"
                        actual = None

                    outcomes.append(
                        {
                            "type": type_name,
                            "identity": (
                                BranchStore._freeze_lifetime_value(identity)
                            ),
                            "ordinal": prediction["ordinal"],
                            "predicted": predicted,
                            "earliest": earliest,
                            "latest": latest,
                            "actual": actual,
                            "status": status,
                        }
                    )
                    cutoff_totals["predictions"] += 1
                    cutoff_totals[status] += 1

            total_predictions += cutoff_totals["predictions"]
            for name in zero_totals:
                global_totals[name] += cutoff_totals[name]
            backtests.append(
                {
                    "cutoff": cutoff,
                    "outcomes": tuple(outcomes),
                    "totals": cutoff_totals,
                }
            )

        if total_predictions > backtest_limit_value:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lifetime churn backtest limit exceeded: "
                f"{total_predictions} prediction records across "
                f"{len(cutoff_values)} cutoff(s), limit is "
                f"{backtest_limit_value}"
            )
        return {
            "backtests": tuple(backtests),
            "totals": global_totals,
        }

def backtests_kwargs(store_args, **overrides) -> dict:
    cutoffs = overrides.pop("cutoffs", ())
    backtest_limit = overrides.pop("backtest_limit", 50)
    kwargs = forecasts_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    kwargs["cutoffs"] = cutoffs
    kwargs["backtest_limit"] = backtest_limit
    return kwargs


def backtests_call(store, store_args, **overrides):
    return store.lifetime_churn_forecast_backtests(
        **backtests_kwargs(store_args, **overrides)
    )


def reference_backtests(
    evolution: dict[str, object],
    min_identities: int,
    max_jitter: int,
    horizon: int,
    cutoffs: tuple[int, ...],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Independently backtest per-cutoff projections against later waves."""
    waves = reference_waves(evolution, min_identities)["waves"]
    observed: dict[tuple[str, object], list[int]] = {}
    for serial, wave in enumerate(waves):
        for member in wave["members"]:
            observed.setdefault(
                (member["type"], member["identity"]), []
            ).append(serial)
    final_serial = len(waves) - 1

    zero = {
        "predictions": 0,
        "hit": 0,
        "early": 0,
        "late": 0,
        "missed": 0,
        "unresolved": 0,
    }
    backtests = []
    totals = dict(zero)
    for cutoff in cutoffs:
        training = waves[: cutoff + 1]
        periodicities = reference_periodicities(
            {"segments": ()}, min_identities, max_jitter
        )
        # Rebuild periodicities from only the cutoff's training waves by
        # filtering each identity's appearances, then projecting.
        per_identity: dict[tuple[str, object], list[int]] = {}
        for serial, wave in enumerate(training):
            for member in wave["members"]:
                per_identity.setdefault(
                    (member["type"], member["identity"]), []
                ).append(serial)

        cutoff_totals = dict(zero)
        outcomes = []
        ordered_keys = []
        records = {}
        for key, serials in per_identity.items():
            if len(serials) < 3:
                continue
            intervals = tuple(b - a for a, b in zip(serials, serials[1:]))
            if max(intervals) - min(intervals) > max_jitter:
                continue
            ordered = sorted(intervals)
            middle = len(ordered) // 2
            period = (
                ordered[middle - 1]
                if len(ordered) % 2 == 0
                else ordered[middle]
            )
            records[key] = (serials[-1], period, min(intervals),
                            max(intervals))
            ordered_keys.append(key)

        # Replicate the periodicity sort order on (jitter, -waves,
        # ... first ascending ...) closely enough for the reference:
        # jitter ascending, participating-wave count descending, first
        # ascending.
        ordered_keys.sort(
            key=lambda key: (
                max(
                    b - a
                    for a, b in zip(
                        per_identity[key], per_identity[key][1:]
                    )
                )
                - min(
                    b - a
                    for a, b in zip(
                        per_identity[key], per_identity[key][1:]
                    )
                ),
                -len(per_identity[key]),
                per_identity[key][0],
            )
        )

        upper = cutoff + horizon
        for key in ordered_keys:
            last, period, smallest, largest = records[key]
            ordinal = 1
            while True:
                wave = last + ordinal * period
                if wave > upper:
                    break
                if wave > cutoff:
                    earliest = last + ordinal * smallest
                    latest = last + ordinal * largest
                    appearances = observed.get(key, ())
                    match = None
                    for serial in appearances:
                        if serial >= earliest:
                            if serial <= latest:
                                match = serial
                            break
                    if match is not None:
                        status = (
                            "hit" if match == wave
                            else "early" if match < wave
                            else "late"
                        )
                        actual = match
                    elif latest <= final_serial:
                        status = "missed"
                        actual = None
                    else:
                        status = "unresolved"
                        actual = None
                    outcomes.append(
                        {
                            "type": key[0],
                            "identity": key[1],
                            "ordinal": ordinal,
                            "predicted": wave,
                            "earliest": earliest,
                            "latest": latest,
                            "actual": actual,
                            "status": status,
                        }
                    )
                    cutoff_totals["predictions"] += 1
                    cutoff_totals[status] += 1
                ordinal += 1

        for name in zero:
            totals[name] += cutoff_totals[name]
        backtests.append(
            {
                "cutoff": cutoff,
                "outcomes": tuple(outcomes),
                "totals": cutoff_totals,
            }
        )

    return {"backtests": tuple(backtests), "totals": totals}

class LifetimeChurnForecastBacktestsStatusTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Exercise every status through synthetic wave membership."""

    @staticmethod
    def _member(type_name, identity, segments=1, added=0, removed=0,
                changed=0):
        return {
            "type": type_name,
            "identity": identity,
            "segments": segments,
            "added": added,
            "removed": removed,
            "changed": changed,
        }

    def _wave(self, serial, members):
        return {
            "from": serial * 2,
            "to": serial * 2 + 1,
            "segments": 1,
            "identities": len(members),
            "added": sum(m["added"] for m in members),
            "removed": sum(m["removed"] for m in members),
            "changed": sum(m["changed"] for m in members),
            "members": tuple(members),
            "changes": (),
        }

    def _build(self, waves, cutoffs, *, max_jitter=0, horizon=10):
        return BranchStore._build_lifetime_churn_backtests_result(
            waves, list(cutoffs), max_jitter, horizon, 100, 100
        )

    def test_hit_early_late_classification_by_first_appearance(self):
        # A appears at waves 0, 1, 2 (steady period 1). Cutoff 2 gives
        # predicted wave 3 with range 3..3. Observed at 3 is a hit; a
        # jittered range 2..4 with first appearance 2 is early and at 4
        # is late.
        base = tuple(
            self._wave(s, (self._member("node", "A"),)) for s in range(3)
        )
        hit_waves = base + (
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        result = self._build(hit_waves, (2,), horizon=2)
        statuses = {
            (o["ordinal"], o["status"]): o
            for o in result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"]
        }
        self.assertEqual(statuses[(1, "hit")]["actual"], 3)

        # Intervals (1, 1) keep earliest == latest, so to get early/late
        # use jitter: A at 0, 2, 3 gives intervals (2, 1), last 3.
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "Z1"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(4, (self._member("node", "Z4"),)),
            self._wave(5, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        # last=3, intervals (2,1), period median=1: ordinal 1 predicts
        # wave 4 with earliest 4, latest 5; first appearance is 5 -> late.
        result = self._build(waves, (3,), horizon=3, max_jitter=1)
        outcomes = result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"]
        first = next(o for o in outcomes if o["ordinal"] == 1)
        self.assertEqual(
            (first["predicted"], first["earliest"], first["latest"]),
            (4, 4, 5),
        )
        self.assertEqual(first["status"], "late")
        self.assertEqual(first["actual"], 5)

    def test_missed_when_interval_fully_observed_without_appearance(self):
        # A at waves 0, 1, 2 then absent; cutoff 2 predicts 3 with range
        # 3..3, and wave 3 is fully observed without A -> missed.
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "Z"),)),
        )
        result = self._build(waves, (2,), horizon=1)
        outcome = result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(outcome["status"], "missed")
        self.assertIsNone(outcome["actual"])
        self.assertEqual(
            result["backtests"][0]["totals"],
            {"predictions": 1, "hit": 0, "early": 0, "late": 0,
             "missed": 1, "unresolved": 0},
        )

    def test_unresolved_when_latest_passes_the_last_observed_wave(self):
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        # Cutoff 2 is the final wave: predicted 3, range 3..3, latest 3
        # is beyond the final observed serial 2 -> unresolved.
        result = self._build(waves, (2,), horizon=1)
        outcome = result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(outcome["status"], "unresolved")
        self.assertIsNone(outcome["actual"])

    def test_appearance_before_earliest_never_matches(self):
        # A at 0, 1, 2 (period 1); jitter via wider intervals is not
        # available, so build a record with intervals (2, 2): A at
        # 0, 2, 4; cutoff 4, ordinal 1 predicts 6, range 6..6. A also
        # appears at wave 5 (before earliest 6) and not at 6; wave 6 is
        # observed, so the wave-5 appearance must not count and the
        # prediction is missed.
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "Z1"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "Z3"),)),
            self._wave(4, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(5, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(6, (self._member("node", "Z6"),)),
        )
        result = self._build(waves, (4,), horizon=3)
        outcome = next(
            o
            for o in result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"]
            if o["ordinal"] == 1
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            (outcome["predicted"], outcome["earliest"],
             outcome["latest"]),
            (6, 6, 6),
        )
        self.assertEqual(outcome["status"], "missed")
        self.assertIsNone(outcome["actual"])

    def test_cutoff_uses_only_its_own_prefix_for_training(self):
        # A appears in waves 0,1,2 and again at 4. At cutoff 2 the
        # steady set trains on 0,1,2 only; wave 3 (no A) is a missed
        # observation and wave 4 is never seen as training.
        waves = (
            self._wave(0, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(1, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(2, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
            self._wave(3, (self._member("node", "Z"),)),
            self._wave(4, (self._member("node", "A"),)),
        )
        result = self._build(waves, (2,), horizon=2)
        by_ordinal = {
            o["ordinal"]: o
            for o in result["backtests"][0]["outcomes"]
        }
        self.assertEqual(by_ordinal[1]["status"], "missed")
        # Ordinal two predicts wave 5; observed only through 4, so it is
        # unresolved even though wave 4 carried an early reappearance
        # (that reappearance belonged to ordinal one's interval and was
        # checked against earliest 3, which it missed).
        self.assertEqual(by_ordinal[2]["status"], "unresolved")
